notes.effect:
A specialty for The Devil Who Laughs Last, this ability should be used quite a bit throughout the battle. It gives the players a sense that this entity isn't just part of the character's world, but exist beyond it. by Breaking the 4th Wall, you can get the player's feeling for their characters, and following through accordingly. Make it personal! Show your players that the characters are something they don't always have control over. While the mechanical effects can be achieved on a personal level, you can use alternative effects that can deeply effect the characters in other ways.

GM: "and now The Devil Who Laugh Last is gonna use..." *pause and visually change attitude for the persona of The Devil*
Devil: "Now, now, now! Hold up a moment. I like to ask THEM something." *point to a player. If the character speaks, have The Devil interject.* "No, no, no! Not YOU! THEM! The one behind you."
Devil: "Tell me stranger, what do you like about this world? about the people in it? about their pointless lives and useless nations vying for territory by shedding blood of those who are ordered to while the fat slobs that are their monarchs and rulers are safe in the back, sitting on their gaudy golden thrones? Tell me your thoughts."
Player: "Um, I think it's nice. Lots of fun NPCs and unique  items all around. I really enjoyed the Kingdom of Soltissa and their festival."
Devil: "Oh, The Kingdom of Soltissa? Isn't that where this little fellow is from?" *points to a different player's character.*
Player: "Yeah, I think they are. I actually developed a Bond with that kingdom because I enjoyed it."
Devil: "I see... Too bad such a place no longer exists" *The Devil snaps his fingers, and the GM switches back to narrating.*
GM: You all feel a sudden pressure, but only for a second, gone as fast as it came. And yet, some of you feel empty inside. Far far away, high in the sky, you all watch as the Kingdom of Soltissa is instantly obliterated - the kingdom walls and every structure flattened into ruins, dust and smoke rising from the suddenly collapse. Adults and children screaming and crying in horror and shock, pained wails as others suffocate and die beneath the rubble they are caught under. Everything is gone. Any character with bonds with that kingdom gain a bond of inferiority and hatred towards The Devil Who Laughs Last, as well as suffer enraged and shaken. *The Devil persona is used again*
Devil "Do you all like my trick? Ha Ha ha ha ha!"

Using Breaking the 4th Wall like this should make the Scene more interesting, while giving both the players and their characters and unique connection, making matters like this more personal as they face The Devil Who Laughs Last.
notes.name: Breaking the 4th Wall

As an action, The Devil Who Laughs Last sings a rhyme that bends the fabric of reality in the battle. When Rhyme Time is used, choose one of the following effects:
• Replace an **Attribute** with another different **Attribute** for all checks. This last for the Scene, or until Rhyme Time is used again.
• All combatants choose two **Attributes** of your choice. One **Attribute** is treated as **one die higher** (to a maximum of **d12**), and the other **Attribute** is treated as **one die lower** (to a minimum of **d6**). This last for the Scene, or until Rhyme Time is used again.
• All instances of **recovery** and **damage** are **reversed**. This last until the end of the round.
• All attacks and spells ignore Resistances, Immunities, and Absorbencies. All neutral Affinities are now treated as Vulnerabilities. This effect last until the end of the round.
• Before taking their action, **all combatants** must sing a rhyme appropriate for the action they are taking. If a combatant fails to sing a rhyme, they suffer any damage and any status effects of their attack, spell or skill. oh7pmjKliWHD0bUsBuvU.description:
A **Shadow** that lives long enough and consumes the hearts of enough living creatures may eventually metamorphose into a **Neoshadow**. 

Driven by the same mindless hunger as their weaker brethren and strengthened by years of feeding on hearts, **Neoshadows** are deadly pack hunters of the dark. Quicker and more mobile than regular **Shadows**, they can disappear into pools of darkness and reappear in unexpected places. 

As predators, they prefer to strike hard at unsuspecting prey; if they can manage it, **Neoshadows** always begin battle with the element of surprise. They hide in pools of darkness, then appear suddenly and use their *Wind Dance* attack to daze their targets. If any prey survive the initial assault, the **Neoshadows** swarm, using numbers and speed to disorient and overwhelm victims. Like **Shadows**, they can flatten into two-dimensional shapes to slip around a target's guard. 

Those experienced in walking the less trodden paths of the worlds are careful to avoid any particularly heavy patches of shadow; not every dark corner harbors a pack of **Neoshadows**, but any dark corner might.


*Original art by Tetsuya Nomura.*
